name: jumbo-drill-boom-pattern
title: Jumbo Drill Boom Pattern
description: A full-bleed ambient background modeling a tunnel drill jumbo drilling a full blast pattern: one boom's drill steel swings to each of 35 numbered collar points across a rock face and plunges in with a hammering jitter, leaving a growing hole, before withdrawing and repositioning to the next collar in a burn-cut sequence.
useWhen: a full-bleed backdrop where the point is a single boom methodically drilling a numbered hole pattern hole-by-hole across a rock face, growing as an uneven cluster outward from center; pick blast-hole-delay-sequence instead when the surface should read as the pattern already drilled and now FIRING in sequence (a grid of holes changing state on a timed delay) rather than the drilling itself, or tricone-bit-teeth when the mechanic should be one bit crushing rock at a single point rather than a pattern of holes across a face.
instruction: Build <JumboDrillBoomPattern paused? children? className? style?> as a full-bleed Canvas 2D background modeling a REAL TUNNEL DRILL JUMBO drilling a full blast pattern — perimeter, lookout, stoping and lifter holes drilled by a boom-mounted percussive rock drill (drifter) before the round is charged and fired. GEOMETRY: 35 collar points (a 5x7 grid) are laid out from the container's smaller dimension with a power-1.6 warp on each axis so spacing compresses near the pattern center and widens toward the perimeter, matching a real burn-cut layout's tighter relief-hole spacing; the 35 grid cells are then sorted once (mulberry32-seeded) by distance-from-center plus a jitter term, giving a fixed DRILLING ORDER that grows as an uneven cluster outward from center rather than a clean scanned row. TIMELINE IS A PURE FUNCTION OF ELAPSED TIME, not an incrementally-stepped simulation: each hole gets a fixed 2.4s cycle (1.8s drill-in eased with easeOutCubic, 0.3s withdraw, 0.3s reposition swing to the next collar), so 35 holes take exactly 84s to drill the full pattern; that is followed by a 3s pause with the complete pattern visible and the boom parked off to the side, then a 4s dissolve where every drilled hole's depth fades back to zero together (standing in for the round being fired and a fresh face exposed), for a 91s total loop period — every value (hole depth, steel extension, boom position) is derived directly from `elapsedMs mod 91000`, so resuming after a tab hide or an IntersectionObserver reactivation is a matter of re-basing the animation clock (`performance.now() - lastSimTime`), never restarting from t0. ROCK FACE: a low-frequency value-noise field on a small fixed 9x6 control-point grid (mulberry32-seeded once at mount, bilinear+smoothstep resampled) is baked into a small offscreen canvas once at mount and rebuilt only on resize or a token change (never per frame), then drawImage-scaled onto the visible canvas every frame; it ramps between --background and --ns-muted. DRILLED HOLES: each collar's current depth (0..1, growing while its hole is actively drilling, held at 1 through withdraw/reposition and while parked, uniformly scaled by (1-dissolveT) during the reset dissolve) draws three layers at that depth's alpha — a --ns-muted spoil-ring, a soft blurred --foreground shadow (shadowColor/shadowBlur, alpha-only, no color decomposition) to keep the puncture legible against a low-contrast light-theme face, and a crisp --foreground fill on top; undrilled collars show a faint --ns-muted ring as the plan reference and disappear once their hole starts drilling. BOOM + STEEL: simple procedural line/rect geometry — a fixed off-canvas base point, a mast line from base to ~86% of the way to the current target collar (interpolated during the 0.3s reposition swing), and a steel segment that plunges past the collar by up to ~2.1x the hole radius as `steelExtend` ramps 0->1 during drill-in and 1->0 during withdraw, retracted to 0 while traveling; during the drill-in phase only, a 12Hz-equivalent two-term sine jitter (2-3px amplitude, PERPENDICULAR to the boom's own direction) shakes the steel — a real drifter hammers at 30-60Hz, deliberately decoupled from that rate per the round's aliasing rule since it is well above what a 60fps canvas can render believably. RESTING LOOP: mount always lands at simTime = 28000ms into the 91000ms loop (~a third of the pattern already drilled, one boom mid-plunge with visible jitter) — real elapsed time then carries it forward from there, so +2.5s shows one more hole complete and the boom mid-swing, +5s shows a visibly larger, still-uneven drilled cluster. prefers-reduced-motion freezes at the fixed simTime 51300ms (~61% through the 84s drill phase, the 22nd hole mid-plunge at exactly half depth) chosen because it is the one frame showing fully drilled holes, one in-progress hole and untouched undrilled collars all at once — the paused prop freezes at whatever simTime the animation last reached rather than snapping back to t0. TOKENS: --foreground (rock structure line-work, boom/steel, hole fill), --ns-muted (ambient noise field, spoil rings, undrilled collar marks) and --background (canvas clear) are read via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) only after document.fonts.ready resolves and before the first paint, gated behind a `ready` flag on every path that could otherwise draw first (ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver, the reduced-motion/paused branch), and re-read (with the rock buffer rebuilt) on a MutationObserver watching documentElement's class. No --ns-accent anywhere — no interaction moment, this is a resting ambient surface; there is no pointer/press/scroll driving movement so autoplay.mode is 'none'. HOST: DPR-capped backing store (max 2), IntersectionObserver (threshold 0) and document visibilitychange both stop the single rAF loop, a debounced ResizeObserver rebuilds the collar layout, holeR/jitter scale and rock buffer on layout change. The canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events-none; children render as real DOM above it in normal focus order and are never intercepted by the canvas. Zero dependencies.
